reviews.review:
Mass Effect Andromeda is a pretty frustrating game because for everything it does well, there is always something else that comes up and hurts the experience. At one moment, the visuals are absolutely stunning while exploring a frozen alien world and the next, I clip through a rock and my vehicle explodes. Sometimes, the combat is insanely fluid, flying around and sniping people in mid air, throwing enemies around with my biotics and swapping my character builds on the fly to best suit myself for the situation, the next, I get stuck on some odd piece of geometry and subsequently die. Sometimes, the facial animations look pretty solid, the next, it looks as if Scott Ryder is a clay statue that just gained sentience and is speaking words for the first time.

That's what this game is, a mixed bag. The writing at times I found to be quite compelling and good at creating a bit of intrigue, only to be ♥♥♥♥ on by a character saying something akin to what a 13 year old would imagine a grown man saying if they were in space talking to a hostile alien race. Really, the only non-mixed bag aspect of this game I experienced were the menus, mainly the research and development menus, which are utter ♥♥♥♥ to be perfectly blunt, as the developers thought it would be a great idea to show every item in the game that is craftable, instead of showing you the items you can actually make with the resources you have.

Despite all this though, I still enjoyed this game. For the most part, the good outweighs the bad. I enjoyed most of the characters. Peebee, Drax, and Vetra being some of my favorites. Cora is fine if a bit one-note, and Liam and Jaal are just pieces of wood, but still have some interesting aspects. I enjoyed, not so much the Archon himself, but the Kett overall as a villainous force. I think the game did a very good job creating a bit of mystery around the Kett and their motivations. I also enjoyed learning about the remnant, even if the remnant vaults could be repetitive and a bit tedious at times. The combat was by far my favorite element of the game. The combat is at its best when you are in wide open spaces with lots of enemies around you. The movement is fluid, the abilities are easy to use and when combined, can make some devastating combos and all the guns feel great. However, the combat is hurt by not being able to order your squad mates around to the same extent as the older games (that is, not being able to order squad mates to use certain abilities at certain times). 

Overall, this game is a solid 6-6.5/10 for me. There is some good fun to be had here and the story is pretty good, even if there is a bit of cheesy or in some cases, downright goofy writing (sequences with Liam particularly come to mind). I think the combat and intrigue around the story is good and it kept me drawn in until the end. And, while I didn't love all the characters, the ones I did love kept me invested. In fact, some of the best character moments are when you bring two characters with you into the Nomad, and see how the interact with and play off one another. 

I recommend this game, with the caveat that it will likely not be a bug-free experience. And if you look to get different things than I do out of these types of games, you may consider skipping this game or waiting until it is heavily discounted.

some ppl say, that it was a bad game, some ppl say, that it was badly optimized.. well.. it is not. it's a rich and very good looking masterpiece. you can feel the "vibe", I envy the heroes - that's something

First off, you have to let go of the trilogy when you play this game if you want to enjoy Andromeda. Just consider the two being relatives, they share some genetics but they don't have the same features in looks and personality. With that said I'm not gonna pretend that this game is great and all worth it. It's however quite good game for those who love exploring with a touch of openworld slash RPG set in space among aliens. The downside(s) could be the lack of creativity in writing that starts showing already before you're halfway into the game especially if you're a nerd for side-quests, but mainly with the shallowness of the characters and above all Ryder. Not gonna criticize the graphics because others have done that already, but yeah I think ME3 character graphics and face mechanics were better. Enough said! I decided to give this game a chance despite the negative reputation only because it was on sale, so if you catch it on a discounted price make sure you grab it, then one can say it's all worth it.
